P1 west flat furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: a central spine (x15) kept clear from the door to the back, with a spruce table and chairs, a stove by the chimney, a red bed at x14 z14..15, and barrels, chest and lanterns on the east side.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks; room check: 7/7 floor cells reachable and min light 12, with no dark cells, FIT OK.
Standalone the walk reports "no way in" because the porch step at [15,1,6] is Fittings' job; with a scratch step added, the room check is OK.
left: Walkability depends on the Fittings part building the porch step: spruce_stairs facing south at x15 y1 z6 (plan: step in each gap). Without it the walk reports 'no way in'; with it (tested on a scratch copy) all cells are reachable and OK.
The party-wall chimney cells x17 z12..13 are still air until P4 builds the chimney, so the walk plan shows them as doorways 'D'. Not my cells; they clear once the chimney exists.

elements.md items 19 (beds) and 20 (tables) are only partly built: this room has one bed (bed() at x14 z14..15) and one table (spruce_fence + spruce_slab top at x14 z12). I did not tick them: they are cross-room items, plan.md has no room checklist, and I did not edit shared files.
Room look: room.png is small, and the table and chairs are hard to read from above. Visually acceptable, but a larger inside-eye view would confirm the focal read.

waste.what: Checked walkability by hand against the 3x6 floor grid before writing the layout; the candidate layout kept failing reachability (pockets cut off by table and chairs), and I redrew it twice.
waste.cost: about 3 layout iterations in head, 0 tool runs
waste.tool: a `mcd room --layout <file>` dry run that takes a layers() legend and rows and reports walk and light before make.sh, so a layout is tested without a full rebuild

waste.what: Verified walkability by writing a scratch copy of build.nbt with the porch step added, because the room check starts from the building entrance and the step is another part's job.
waste.tool: `mcd room --assume-step` or a `--from x,y,z` option on `mcd room` / `mcd walk` to start the flood from the room's own door cell, so each interior designer can check their room without other parts

waste.what: Worked out the lantern standing heights and the table top slab placement (fence top at y4.5, top slab in cell y4, lantern at y5) by reasoning instead of a helper.
waste.cost: a few minutes of reasoning, 0 retries
waste.tool: a `table(g, x, z, wood)` vocab helper (fence post + top slab, with an optional lantern on top) and a `chair(g, x, z, facing, wood)` helper

companions.task: Build the porch step at x15 y1 z6 (spruce_stairs facing south) and the front door at x15 z9, so the room is reachable from the lane; that is the one thing the room check needs from outside.
Build the party-wall chimney at x17..18 z12..13 so the east wall closes, with the stove at x16 z12 against its face.
Check the whole row's lantern levels once the porch lanterns and the lane lamps are in, so the front room light isn't counted on alone.
